Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...

immediately.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

A strong low pressure system off the Pacific Coast will begin to draw
in tropical moisture associated with Topical Storm Rachel this
weekend. This strong southerly fetch will draw anomalously high
moisture content across the Desert Southwest and into eastern Utah
and western Colorado. The chance for widespread precipitation
increases Saturday evening into Sunday. Total precipitation forecasts
range from 1 to 3 inches across high terrain, with highest amounts
favoring the Uintas, Tavaputs and the Southwest San Juan mountains.

Embedded thunderstorms are also possible Sunday afternoon, increasing
the threat for flash flooding across vulnerable terrain. While
confidence in location and rainfall rates remain low at this time,
the potential for rapidly rising rivers, streams, normally dry
arroyos and slot canyons are possible Sunday through Monday.

Please follow the evolving forecast, especially if your plans
including recreating or commuting across eastern Utah and western
Colorado Sunday onward. Also, keep in mind weather potential above
your location and upstream, particularly for those who reside below
sensitive terrain like recent burn scars.

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Waters From Point Grenville To Cape Shoalwater 10 To 60 Nm
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 9 at 8:54AM PDT until October 10 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, northwest winds 20 to 30 kt with
gusts to 35 kt. For the Small Craft Advisory, north winds 20 to
30 kt and seas 9 to 13 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters From Point Grenville To Cape Shoalwater
10 To 60 Nm.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 11 PM PDT this evening. For
the Small Craft Advisory, from 11 PM this evening to 6 PM PDT
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

NWSheadline: GALE WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 PM PDT THIS EVENING... ...SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 11 PM THIS EVENING TO 6 PM PDT SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Grays Harbor Bar
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 9 at 8:54AM PDT until October 10 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Rough bar conditions. Combined seas 6 to 8 ft rising to 9
to 11 ft this afternoon. Seas easing to 7 to 9 ft Saturday
morning.

* WHERE...Grays Harbor Bar.

* WHEN...From 2 PM this afternoon to 5 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft
especially when navigating in or near harbor entrances.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Maximum ebb currents will occur
around 400 AM and 430 PM today and 445 AM Saturday. The
afternoon ebb will be strong.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory for rough bar means that wave conditions
are expected to be hazardous to small craft in or near harbor
entrances.

NWSheadline: SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 2 PM THIS AFTERNOON TO 5 AM PDT SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Admiralty Inlet
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 9 at 8:54AM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Northwest winds 20 to 30 kt.

* WHERE...Admiralty Inlet.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 21 to 33 knots
and/or seas 10 feet or higher are expected to produce hazardous
wave conditions to small craft. Inexperienced mariners,
especially those operating smaller vessels should avoid
navigating in these conditions.
